methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: The AI Age — meeting the moment - Virginia Business
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Business convening a major AI discourse signals business community engagement, but framing as 'meeting the moment' suggests capability-building is still aspirational and likely concentrating where existing tech infrastructure exists rather than distributing equitably.

signals.title: NoVA Leaders Debate Data Centers, Metro Funding And The Housing Crisis - Patch
signals.signal_reading: Data centers outbidding home builders for land in NoVA demonstrates how AI infrastructure investment concentrates in existing tech corridors while creating secondary tensions (housing crisis) that may limit workforce distribution and deepen regional inequality.

signals.title: Norfolk could get AI assist for non-emergency calls - WAVY.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk deploying AI for non-emergency call dispatch represents shallow, platform-delivered adoption in municipal services—practical efficiency gains without deep capability-building, signaling distributed but thin AI integration outside tech hubs.

signals.title: Virginia Beach schools bring ChatGPT under division oversight as AI use grows - 13newsnow.com
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Beach schools bringing ChatGPT under division oversight indicates shallow, platform-dependent adoption where institutions consume AI tools rather than develop indigenous capability, distributed geographically but not building deep technical fluency.

signals.title: Southwest Field Notes: National Black Lung Association to meet next week in Abingdon amid historic high numbers of the disease in central Appalachia
signals.signal_reading: Black lung disease meeting in Abingdon juxtaposed with a data center public hearing reveals Southwest's struggle between legacy economic burdens and new tech infrastructure—neither deep AI capability nor equitable distribution is materializing in coal-transition communities.
